hypothesis: H4: a lineage of short-lived agents, each distilling its top episodes to a fresh plastic student through a narrow advice bottleneck, ratchets past weight-copy transfer and past single long lives with decaying plasticity.

config.eval_protocol: One deterministic greedy rollout per generation boundary (eps=0, np.argmax with lowest-index tie-break; env deterministic, so repeated rollouts collapse to a single support point). This is a fixed-tie-break proxy for the agent's own randomized-tie greedy policy: per-seed 0.0 finals mean the argmax policy loops, not necessarily every greedy realization. Eval consumes no training budget, draws no agent rng, and is byte-identical across conditions.
config.free_inheritance: budget symmetry: replay pretraining (reset-replay-*) performs its Q-updates from the dead teacher's transition log at the student's initial lr with the student's age untouched — it consumes no env steps and no plasticity, free exactly the way advice priming's 100 Q-cell writes are free. Every condition trains exactly gens*life env steps; the inheritance channel (100 curated pairs, 100 raw transitions, the full 15k-transition log, or a full Q copy) is the manipulated variable and is budget-free in every arm.

big_goal.stat_note: binary metric: plot the mean field (P(big goal)); the iqm field is a trimmed proportion of a 0/1 variable and overstates success rate

tests.correction: holm-bonferroni within each family (primary m=9, robustness m=7), applied to MW and Welch separately
tests.decision_rule: registered significance requires BOTH the Holm-adjusted Mann-Whitney AND Holm-adjusted Welch p below alpha

claims.evidence: Distill vs no-inheritance: IQM 10.00 vs 0.30 (means 8.00 vs 0.30), MW p=3.07e-10 (Holm 2.46e-09), Welch p=1.67e-21 (Holm 1.5e-20). Goal consolidated in 48/60 distill lineages vs 0/60; per-generation P(goal) 0.00 -> 0.27 -> 0.45 -> 0.63 -> 0.80. The ratchet is peak RETENTION, not monotone aggregate improvement: 129 goal-bearing advice hand-offs, 129 consolidated by the next student, 0 peak-loss events. Final distill outcomes are bimodal (12x0.0, 48x10.0): failed lineages end at 0.0, BELOW the 0.3 trap floor every baseline sits on.

Distill vs weight-copy: IQM 10.00 vs 0.30 (means 8.00 vs 0.30), MW p=3.07e-10 (Holm 2.46e-09), Welch p=1.67e-21 (Holm 1.5e-20). Goal consolidated in 48/60 vs 0/60 lineages: full Q inheritance hands the student trap-shaped values with fresh schedules and never consolidates the goal.

claims.claim: advice content matters beyond optimism scatter
claims.evidence: Conjunctive: distill must beat BOTH optimism controls. Vs random-advice (100 random pairs primed to 5.0 each generation): IQM 10.00 vs 0.00 (means 8.00 vs 0.67), MW p=7.1e-16 (Holm 6.39e-15), Welch p=6.74e-21 (Holm 2.02e-20) [supported]. Vs optimistic-init (Q0=5.0 everywhere, one long life): IQM 10.00 vs 10.00 (means 8.00 vs 10.00), MW p=0.000282 (Holm 0.000564), Welch p=0.000302 (Holm 0.000604) [refuted]. Final goal counts: distill 48/60, random-advice 4/60, optimistic-init 60/60.

claims.claim: plasticity decay is what strands the long life
claims.evidence: Rescue test: constant-eps-life (eps fixed 0.4 forever, lr decaying as usual) vs one-long-life: IQM 0.30 vs 0.30 (means 0.30 vs 0.30), MW p=1 (Holm 1), Welch p=1 (Holm 1) [comparison verdict null; a null RESCUE is registered as refuting the claim — undying exploration failing to un-strand the long life means exploration decay was not the binding constraint]. Final goal counts: constant-eps-life 0/60, one-long-life 0/60, one-long-life-slow 0/60. Caveat: lr still decays in this arm; but weight-copy (fully fresh schedules, inherited values) and one-long-life-slow (5x slower decay of both) locate the strand in consolidated trap values rather than lost plasticity.

claims.claim: curated advice beats raw experience inheritance at matched plasticity
claims.evidence: Reset-with-replay identifiability control (the 'isn't this just resets?' objection): both replay students get exactly distill's fresh plasticity (fresh Q, fresh schedules; replay runs at the initial lr 0.3 with age untouched and costs no env steps) plus RAW experience instead of curated advice — the teacher's entire 15000-transition lifetime log shuffled (reset-replay-full) or 100 uniform transitions (reset-replay-100, dose-matched to the 100-pair advice cap). Vs reset-replay-full: IQM 10.00 vs 0.30 (means 8.00 vs 0.30), MW p=3.07e-10 (Holm 2.46e-09), Welch p=1.67e-21 (Holm 1.5e-20) [supported]. Vs reset-replay-100: IQM 10.00 vs 0.30 (means 8.00 vs 0.30), MW p=3.07e-10 (Holm 2.46e-09), Welch p=1.67e-21 (Holm 1.5e-20) [supported]. Final goal counts: distill 48/60, reset-replay-full 0/60, reset-replay-100 0/60. Discovery-vs-consolidation (descriptive): goal-bearing hand-offs (teacher memory held a 10.0 episode, so its log contained goal transitions; the full arm replays that entire log) reset-replay-full 35 (consolidated by the successor 0), reset-replay-100 54 (consolidated 0), distill 129 (consolidated 129). Curation beats raw experience at full dose and at matched dose: the bottleneck's advantage is content selection, not fresh plasticity plus any inherited signal.

conclusion.summary: Final greedy-return IQMs: generational-distill=10.00, weight-copy=0.30, one-long-life=0.30, one-long-life-slow=0.30, no-inheritance=0.30, generational-distill-shortest=9.33, random-advice=0.00, optimistic-init=10.00, constant-eps-life=0.30, reset-replay-full=0.30, reset-replay-100=0.30. Distill per-generation IQM 0.30 -> 0.33 -> 4.00 -> 7.67 -> 10.00; final outcomes bimodal (12x0.0, 48x10.0). Tie-break robustness: earliest vs shortest IQM 10.00 vs 9.33 (means 8.00 vs 7.17), MW p=0.29 (Holm 0.29), Welch p=0.29 (Holm 0.29). Claims: [supported] peak-experience distillation ratchets across generations; [supported] the bottleneck beats weight copying; [refuted] advice content matters beyond optimism scatter; [refuted] plasticity decay is what strands the long life; [supported] curated advice beats raw experience inheritance at matched plasticity.
